svg.text: FORMAT LINEAGE: Eugene Yan • Shreya Shankar • MT-Bench (Zheng et al. 2023)
Before You Quote a Judge Score: Calibrate It Like a Lab Instrument
A judge is only as good as its agreement with humans on cases where you know the answer. Example: 100 hand-labeled traces, one binary judge.
Numbers are an example calibration set; re-run yours every release.
5 KNOWN JUDGE BIASES → THE FIX THAT ACTUALLY WORKS
A model rates its own outputs
ask the judge to verify step
JUDGE PROMPT SKELETON (COPY, THEN FILL THE RUBRIC)
SYSTEM: You grade one criterion only.
CRITERION: <one failure mode, e.g. 'fabricated tool result'>
PASS = every claimed action has a matching tool call
FAIL = any claimed action lacks a tool call
DO NOT reward length, tone, or politeness.
Every release: re-grade 50 human-labeled traces; alert if TPR or
TNR drops more than 5 points; keep 20% of labels hidden from
Watch TNR (does the judge catch real failures?) — a lenient judge quietly inflates every dashboard.
MT-Bench: GPT-4 agreed with humans ~80%, the same as humans with each
other — but showed position, verbosity, and self-enhancement bias.
Who Validates the Validators: humans' criteria drift as they grade;
Hamel Husain: binary pass/fail beats Likert; validate judges with
If you cannot show the confusion matrix, you do not have a judge — you have an opinion generator.
